prompt: A TBP volume percent is weighted by volume share when two crudes are blended. What is the reason?
options: Volume is conserved on mixing and mass is not, so every property of a blend, sulfur included, has to be weighted on volume shares.
A TBP yield is a volume fraction, a percent of the barrels, and a volume fraction of a blend is weighted by volume shares.
The engine holds no gravity for a crude at the curve step, so a volume share is the only weight it can form for the yields there.
A volume weighting gives the larger blend yield at every temperature, which is the conservative reading.
explanation: Each property is weighted on the basis it is expressed on: sulfur, a mass fraction, on mass shares; a yield, a volume fraction, on volume shares. The engine can weight yields on mass: SECTION 15 prints blendOnMass beside them.
